rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an supplies people with many novel, clear, firmly grounded examples, phrased more elegantly than ordinary parables.
rows.anchor: من كل مثل } أي معنى غريب هو أوضح وأثبت من أعلام الجبال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even a clear miracle beyond what unbelievers demanded would be called falsehood by those whose hearts God has sealed; believers would affirm it.
rows.anchor: ليقولن الذين كفروا } أي حكمنا بكفرهم غلظة وجفاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God seals the hearts of those unwilling to learn what they do not know, content with ignorance mislabeled as proofs and misguidance mislabeled as guidance.
rows.anchor: لا يجددون - أي لعدم القابلية - العلم بأن لا يطلبوا علم ما يجهلونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is to endure hostile rejection and abuse because all of it remains within God’s will.
rows.anchor: على إنذارهم مع هذا الجفاء والرد بالباطل والأذى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s promise is certainly true, including the Prophet’s victory, the dominance of Islam, and victory for adherents of originally revealed scripture over those without a scripture; time will reveal it.
rows.anchor: الذي منه نصرك وإظهار دينك على الدين كله ونصر من قارب اتباعك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet must not be shaken into hastening victory or slackening in proclamation; he should remain firm and uncompromising toward hostile unbelievers.
rows.anchor: أي يحملنك على الخفة ويطلب أن تخف باستعجال النصر خوفا من عواقب تأخيره

rows.speaker: رويس عن يعقوب
rows.claim: An alternate reading, يستحقنك, from ḥaqq, is understood as not seeking a just settlement from the opponents oneself; the author relates it to worldly concessions that could encourage them to demand favoritism.
rows.anchor: من الحق معناها : أي لا يطلب منك الحق الذي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The standard heavy-nūn reading addresses the foundations of religion: do nothing that gives the opponents hope that the Prophet will incline toward them; the emphatic prohibition is stronger than a bare prohibition.
rows.anchor: فقراءة الجماعةة مصوبة إلى أصل الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who lack settled belief may be wavering doubters or deniers of divine support; they even risked their credibility by confidently expecting Persia to defeat Rome, though God promised Rome’s victory.
rows.anchor: أنهم ليخاطرون ي وعد الله بنصر الروم على فارس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Romans’ promised victory exposed the doubters’ error, and the promised Hour will likewise bring justice for wrongdoers and reward for the virtuous.
rows.anchor: أن الوعد بالساعة لإقامة العدل على الظالم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The close of al-Rūm links back to its opening like an intimate beloved pair, with the ending joined closely to the beginning.
rows.anchor: فقد انعطف آخرها على أولها عطف الحبيب على الحبيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Luqmān’s central purpose is to establish the Book’s wisdom, which entails God’s wisdom in His words and acts; Luqmān’s story demonstrates it.
rows.anchor: مقصودها إثبات الحكمة للكتاب اللازم منه حكمة منولة سبحانه في أقواله وأفعاله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the cycle ending with al-Rūm, Luqmān begins a larger new cycle, paralleling Yūnus: it presents the Qur’an as wise and adds guidance for those who excel; the God-fearing mark beginnings and the excellent mark ends.
rows.anchor: فوصفه في أول هذه التالية للروم بما وصفه به في يونس التالية لغزو الروم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Luqmān’s central purpose is to establish the Book’s wisdom, which entails God’s wisdom in His words and acts; Luqmān’s story demonstrates it.
rows.anchor: مقصودها إثبات الحكمة للكتاب اللازم منه حكمة منولة سبحانه في أقواله وأفعاله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After al-Rūm, a larger new cycle begins, paralleling Yūnus: the Qur’an is wise and also guidance for those who excel, while the God-fearing are people of beginnings and the excellent people of ends.
rows.anchor: وذلك الوصف هو الحكمة وزاد أنه هدى وهداية للمحسنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Luqmān’s story recalls his gratitude in himself and his instruction of his son; repudiating shirk is the highest gratitude, and his example teaches patience, thankfulness, persistence in good, and child-rearing.
rows.anchor: ما يدل على شكره في نفسه وأمره به لغيره فإنه لا شكر يعدل البراءة من الشرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Luqmān admonishes his son with counsel that benefits, softens the heart, disciplines the soul, and produces reverence and justice; the wording suggests repeated admonition.
rows.anchor: أي يوصيه بما ينفعه ويرقق قلبه ويهذب نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The affectionate address ‘my son’ expresses tenderness and compassion to make the counsel more acceptable.
rows.anchor: بأحب ما يخاطب به , مع إظهار الترحم والتحنن والشفقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Correct belief comes before sound action; the prohibition covers both manifest and hidden forms of associating partners with God.
rows.anchor: أي لا توقع الشرك لا جليا ولا خفيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shirk is grave injustice because it puts things out of place, especially by equating a dependent creature with the Necessary Being, from whom every blessing comes; it contradicts wisdom.
rows.anchor: أي فهو ضد الحكمة , لأنه وضع الشيء في غير محله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The counsel warns Quraysh and every listener that a wise father would not depart from it; its consequence is security and guidance, the great religious and worldly blessings.
rows.anchor: وفي هذا تنبيه لقريش وكل سامع على أن هذه وصية لا يعدل عنها

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reports that the Companions were distressed by the ‘injustice’ in 6:82; the Prophet explained it by citing Luqmān’s statement that shirk is grave injustice. The author calls the report sound in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī.
rows.anchor: كما هو صحيح البخاري في غير موضع عن عبدالله بن مسعود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God follows the warning against shirk with a command to honor parents, a secondary means of one’s existence and upbringing, magnifying their right and showing that gratitude to God entails gratitude to people.
rows.anchor: أتبعه سبحانه وصيته للولد بالوالد لكونه المنعم الثاني

rows.speaker: أبو الدرداء
rows.claim: A report in al-Firdaws attributed to Abū al-Dardāʾ says a servant who fulfilled every obligation except filial piety would not enter Paradise; honoring parents orders the practices of monotheism, prayer, and remembrance. No grading is stated.
rows.anchor: كما في الفردوس عن أبي الدرداء رضي الله عنه أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parent’s right does not license obedience in shirk: the son must refuse that command, since it opposes wisdom and the child must prioritize the greater duty while avoiding the lesser harm.
rows.anchor: وتحريم امتثال الابن لذلك ووجوب مخالفته لأبيه فيه تقديما لأعظم الحقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mother is especially honored for the distinctive hardships of carrying, sustaining, and raising the child, which the father does not bear in the same way.
rows.anchor: مما حصل لها من المشقة بسببه وما لها إليه من التربية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Weakness upon weakness’ portrays the mother carrying the child amid her own inherent weakness, compounded as pregnancy advances.
rows.anchor: أي حال كونها ذات وهن تحمله في أحشائها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fīṣāl means weaning after birth; the mother’s tender care is a special favor to a child who can do nothing for himself.
rows.anchor: أي فطامه من الرضاعة بعد وضعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two nursing years involve hardship in sleep and waking known fully only to God; calling them ‘years’ also reflects the parents’ joy in even the child’s most demanding early care.
rows.anchor: تقاسي فيهما في منامه وقيامه ما لا يعلمه حق علمه إلا الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition fī suggests parents may wean before the full two years when the child’s condition and welfare call for it.
rows.anchor: مشيرا إلى أن الوالدين لهما أن يفطماه قبل تمامهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to give thanks explains God’s charge: He is the true giver, while parents are causes He appointed for one’s existence and upbringing.
rows.anchor: أي أوجد هذه الحقيقة ولتكن من همك

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī compares creation to a tree whose fruit is the human being, its kernel rather than rind, and its completion; the human combines features of the two worlds and receives verbal revelation.
rows.anchor: من لوامعه : الموجودات كلها كالشجرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘To Me is the return’ warns that God will question people about their parents’ rights; neglected parents can make their claim before God.
rows.anchor: أي فأسألك عن ذلك كما كانت منهما البداءة ظاهرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In 31:15, ‘strive against you’ with ʿalā signals forceful parental pressure; 29:8 speaks more generally of trial, and its wording hints that coerced verbal assent need not remove faith though it forfeits the description of excellence here.
rows.anchor: وأشار بأداة الاستعلاء إلى أنه لا مطمع لمن أطاعهما في ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No branch of knowledge supports shirk; reason and prophetic transmission affirm divine oneness. The purported ‘unity’ of the heretical ittiḥād doctrine exceeds reason and contradicts revelation.
rows.anchor: بل العلوم كلها دالة على الوحدانية على الوجه الذي تطابقت عليه العقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The son must not obey even both parents if they press him to associate partners with God; their demand is unjust and foolish, a warning against Quraysh’s imitation of their ancestors.
rows.anchor: أي في ذلك ولو اجتمعا على المجاهدة لك عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Refusing the parents’ demand to sin does not mean abandoning them in every other matter; the passage is about the specific conflict over religion.
rows.anchor: قد يفهم الإعراض عنهما رأسا في كل أمر إذا خالفا في الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the advice on gratitude, shirk, and parents, the account returns to Luqmān’s wisdom: God knows and accounts for even the smallest deed, reinforcing monotheism.
rows.anchor: حسن جدا الرجوع إلى تمام بيان حكمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The affectionate ‘my son’ also stresses how insignificant a child is beside bearing God’s wrath; the feminine pronoun can refer to an act, or to obedience, disobedience, good, or evil.
rows.anchor: متحببا مستعطفا , مصغرا له بالنسبة إلى حمل شيء من غضب الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority read miṯqāla ḥabbatin min khardalin with khardal accusative; the two Medinan readers raise it, construing the clause as the existence of some tiny thing at some time.
rows.anchor: هذا على قراءة الجمهور بالنصب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dropping the nūn in in tak emphasizes brevity and the tiniest possible existence; retaining it in fa-takun stresses the deed’s persistence in its location.
rows.anchor: وأسقط النون لغرض الإيجار في الإيصاء بما ينيل المفاز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mustard seed is the least thing likely to come to mind; even if hidden in any rock, across the immense heavens, or anywhere on earth, God brings it forth. Repeated aw marks each realm individually without excluding overlap.
rows.anchor: أي صخرة كانت ولو أنها أشد الصخور وأقواها وأصغرها وأخفاها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God brings even the hidden tiny deed itself into account; His subtle reach and exhaustive knowledge explain why nothing can escape Him.
rows.anchor: بعظم جلاله , وباهر كبريائه وكماله , بعينها لا يخفى عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer is to be performed with all its limits and conditions; it saves and purifies the self and restrains wrongdoing because it turns toward the One God and away from all else.
rows.anchor: أي بجميع حدودها وشروطها ولا تغفل عنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer is second only to monotheism; the omission of almsgiving here signals Luqmān’s and his son’s detachment from worldly provision.
rows.anchor: ولهذا الإقبال والإعراض كانت ثانية التوحيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Enjoining right completes one’s duty to others and is more comprehensive than merely forbidding wrong, since forbidding wrong does not itself entail performing good.
rows.anchor: عطف على ذلك تكميله لنفسه بتكميل غيره توفية لحق الخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People on life’s journey must protect companions: wrongdoing corrupts the shared vessel, and neglecting to restrain its corrupter can drown everyone.
rows.anchor: وكان فساد السفينة مغرقا لكل من فيها

rows.speaker: أبو الأسود الدؤلي
rows.claim: Abū al-Aswad’s verse says to begin by correcting oneself; after one’s own soul gives up wrongdoing, one may rightly be called wise.
rows.anchor: أبي الأسود رحمه الله تعالى : ابدأ بنفسك فانهها عن غيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sequence ‘patience and prayer’ in 2:45 differs because its addressees are unbelievers engrossed in worldly things, while Luqmān’s addressee is a believing ascetic.
rows.anchor: واختلاف المخاطب في الموضعين أوجب اختلاف الترتيبين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The counsel ends with patience, the key to all actions and abstentions.
rows.anchor: وجعل ختامه الصبر الذي هو ملاك الأعمال والتروك كلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘That is among the matters requiring resolve’ names the counsel, especially patience, as decisive and obligatory matters on which one must be fully set; no religious community has leave to abandon them.
rows.anchor: أي الأمور المقطوع بها المفروضة أو القاطعة الجازمة بجزم فاعلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worship and commanding right can breed conceit and arrogance; the warning against turning one’s cheek signals that gentle conduct, not harshness, is wanted.
rows.anchor: لتصورهما بصورة الاستعلاء - الإعجاب إلى الكبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person entrusted with something who preserves it and gives it to its rightful recipients is faithful and discharges the trust; one who withholds or ruins it is a traitorous bearer of it.
rows.anchor: فحفظه ورعاه وبذله لأهله وآتاه باذلا للأمانة غير حامل لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gave people reason to distinguish right from wrong and faculties for obedience or sin; those who use them rightly discharge the trust, while most do the opposite. The created world likewise offers its benefits.
rows.anchor: أودع الناس من العقول ما يميزون به بين الصحيح والفاسد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The trust is obedience to God in what He commands rational beings and what He wills from other creatures; the verse names the heavens, earth, and mountains to make the offer comprehensive.
rows.anchor: وهي طاعته سبحانه فيما أمر به العاقل , وفيما أراده من غيره

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī explains ‘bearing the trust’ as retaining what is due to another until it leaves one’s liability; the burden rides its bearer, like debt, until payment.
rows.anchor: من قولك : فلان حامل للأمانة ومحتمل لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cosmos’ refusal and awe mean each part delivers what God deposited in it at the appointed time, like the creatures’ ‘we come willingly’ response.
rows.anchor: أتينا طائعين , والحاصل أنه جعلت الإرادة وهي الأمر التكويني

rows.speaker: البغوي عن الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Baghawī, citing al-Zajjāj and other semanticists, explains the comparison: creative command applies to nonrational creatures, while moral command applies to humans who can understand and distinguish; each is judged according to its rank.
rows.anchor: وهذا هو معنى ما نقله البغوي عن الزجاج وغيره من أهل المعاني

rows.speaker: النابغة زياد بن معاوية الذبياني
rows.claim: Al-Nābigha’s cited lines attest faithful keeping of a trust; Ibn al-Furāt reports ʿUmar judged him the most eloquent of their poets.
rows.anchor: وما أحسن ما قاله النابغة زياد بن معاوية الذيباني حيث قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘The human’ refers to most people (and jinn), not every individual: the collective can include jinn, as in 7:85, and a generic singular does not quantify every member.
rows.anchor: والإسناد إلى الجنس لا يلزم منه أن يكون كل فرد منه كذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human self-love and intelligence can make people imagine they have no defects, but desire obscures reason: most become unjust by misplacing things and ignorant as passion overtakes them, except those God protects.
rows.anchor: أي في جبلته إلا من عصم الله

none: Bare heading for the next surah only.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is told to steady believers against numerous opponents by addressing them as God’s servants, an intimate possessive that reassures them of His nearness and honors them.
rows.anchor: يا عباد الله , مثلا تذكيرا لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Belief may exist at its lowest degree without full God-consciousness; ‘fear your Lord’ calls the graced believers to deepen obedience and sincerity, rooting faith and excellence without implying God needs anything.
rows.anchor: وهذا أدل دليل على أن الإيمان يكون مع عدم التقوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers reading ‘for those who excel in this world, a good reward’ as covering good in this life and the Hereafter; an alternative makes only the worldly reward the predicate, unduly limiting the promise.
rows.anchor: أوقعوا الإحسان , ومعلوم أنه في هذه الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative parsing takes aḥsanū to mean ‘did good,’ with ‘in this world’ introducing a new subject-predicate clause; the author rejects it as confined to worldly reward.
rows.anchor: خاصا بثواب الدنيا , فالأول حسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If one’s land obstructs obedience and encourages sin, one should migrate; every land is equally under God’s knowledge and power, so staying put is no excuse for neglecting excellence.
rows.anchor: على الهجرة إلى حيث يزول عنه ذلك المانع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Patience through migration and separation from home or family earns an immeasurable reward: other deeds can be counted, but patience continues with every breath and varies in hidden strength and effects.
rows.anchor: أي على ما تكرهه النفوس في مخالفة الهوى واتباع أوامر الملك الأعلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, perfect patience may mean no reckoning at all; al-Bazzār and Ibn Ḥibbān in his Ṣaḥīḥ transmit from Abū Hurayra that a woman asked the Prophet for a cure and chose patience when told she could have either, receiving no reckoning.
rows.anchor: لما رواه البزار وابن حبان في صحيحه عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet must model sincere worship for the community: the passive ‘I was commanded’ presents the order as settled and irrevocable, and a leader’s precedence encourages others.
rows.anchor: وبني الفعل لما لم يسم فاعله تعظيما للأمر بأنه قطع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worship is sincerely directed to God, the creator of all; being first among Muslims means either highest in rank or earliest in his own time, with this order serving precedence.
rows.anchor: أي المنقادين في الرتبة الحائزين قصب السبق بكل اعتبار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet fears punishment if he disobeys despite divine assurances, from reverence for the Lord who nurtures and favors him; the greatness of the Day makes its punishment still more immense.
rows.anchor: أي مع تأمينه لي بغفران ما تقدم وما تأخر إخلاصا في إجلاله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Good and evil differ both among acts of the same kind and in their agents’ intentions and effort; this comparison urges people toward good and away from evil.
rows.anchor: أي وإن اجتهدت في التحرير والاعتبار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One should repel whatever harm may come from oneself or others with the best attainable conduct; forgiving an offender is good, while responding with benevolence is better.
rows.anchor: أي كل ما يمكن أن يضرك من نفسك ومن الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Such excellent treatment can turn even a bitter enemy into a close friend who readily meets needs, eases difficulties, heals hurts, and removes what is foul, like hot water cleansing dirt.
rows.anchor: عظيمة قد ملأت ما بين البنيين فاجأته حال كونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Answering injury with the best response, beyond forgiveness, forbearance, and patience, serves all the interests of religion and worldly life, but it is contrary to human disposition and must be sought from God.
rows.anchor: التي هي مقابلة الإساءة بأحسن الحسن وهو الإحسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated passive ‘it is granted’ emphasizes that God enables the patient to acquire this virtue; the shift from plural ‘those who are patient’ to singular ‘one of great fortune’ stresses its rarity and rank.
rows.anchor: وكرر إظهار البناء للمفعول للتنبيه على أنه لا قدرة عليها أصلا إلا بتوفيق الخالق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person granted this virtue has an immense share and standing with God and people in this life and the next.
rows.anchor: أي جليل في الدنيا والآخرة عند الله وعند الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional ‘if Satan provokes you’ applies generally to human nature though the Prophet is protected; Satan may still imagine he can tempt him.
rows.anchor: مع العلم بأنه صلى الله عليه وسلم معصوم إشارة إلى رتبة الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb nzagh depicts Satan goading or pricking someone into harmful conduct, as though a person acted irrationally under a painful prod.
rows.anchor: أي ينخسنك ويطعننك طعنا مفسدا فيحصل لك تألم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seek God’s protection immediately at the first impulse: an unchecked thought becomes an idea, resolve, lapse, hardened heart, and persistent sin.
rows.anchor: أي استجر بالملك الأعلى واطلب منه الدخول في عصمته

rows.speaker: القشيري
rows.claim: Al-Qushayrī warns that if the first intrusive thought is not resisted, it develops through deliberation and resolve into a lapse, then hardening and persistence.
rows.anchor: نبه عليه القشيري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah demonstrates the warnings stated plainly and the glad tidings suggested in Sūrat Qāf, especially its ending about worldly calamity and punishment in the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: مقصودها الدلالة على صدق ما أنذرت به سورة ق تصريحا وبشرت به تلويحا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its name, al-Dhāriyāt, points to the oath’s answer; the oath and its five verses cohere so tightly they are like one verse, and the scattering winds aptly signal the warning.
rows.anchor: واسمها الذاريات ظاهر في ذلك بملاحظة جواب القسم فإنه مع القسم لشدة الارتباط كالآية الواحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People deny warnings because they do not perceive their causes, though invisible winds scatter vapor and God gathers and drives it into clouds, producing lightning, thunder, rain, hail, snow, fire, and other marvels that bring joy or distress.
rows.anchor: فإن تكذيبهم بالوعيد لكونهم لا يشعرون بشيء من أسبابه وإن كانت موجودة معهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People can recognize clouds that will rain and those that will not, yet the angels direct all such causes at God’s command; on hearing thunder one is taught to glorify the true disposer of affairs.
rows.anchor: وكل ذلك بتصريف الملائكة عن أمر الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The basmala invokes the perfect God who never fails His promise, the Merciful whose gift of existence reaches all creation, and the Compassionate who guides His chosen to what pleases Him.
rows.anchor: الذي عم الخلائق بنعمة الإيجاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only those turned aside are diverted from the truth; the author describes this as an easy, decisive reversal fixed in the eternal decree, leaving their words and deeds unable to stay on the straight course.
rows.anchor: أي يصرف بأيسر أمر وأسهله عن سنن الاستقامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Perish the conjecturers’ condemns liars, fabricators, and people who speak by guesswork without scripture, Prophetic practice, or transmitted knowledge; the phrase is an imprecation or declaration of their due destruction.
rows.anchor: أي حصل بأيسر أمر قتل الكذابين ولا محالة من كل قاتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those in a ‘deep immersion’ are submerged in blindness, error, intoxication, and ignorance, as unstable as someone walking in the open sea; their speech, conduct, and states are disordered.
rows.anchor: أي أعماق من العمى والضلال , غارقون في سكرهم وجهلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heedless are forgetful, distracted, bewildered, and pulled away from what matters, displaying conflicting dispositions under distress.
rows.anchor: أي عريقون في السهو وهو النسيان والغفلة والحيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their repeated, mocking question about the Day of Recompense demonstrates their heedlessness; even human masters inspect their servants’ work, so the Most Wise would not leave His ordered creation purposeless or unrewarded.
rows.anchor: أي حينا بعد حينا بعد حين على سبيل الاستمرار استهزاء
